title: Neural Networks — Pass a Row Through a Layer
key_insight: Put the inputs in a vector and the weights in a matrix. Matrix multiplication computes all weighted connections together, then a bias shifts each result.
body:
## Pass a Row Through a Layer

A layer receives several input numbers and must produce several new numbers. Doing every connection separately would be slow and hard to track.

Put the inputs in a vector and the weights in a matrix. Matrix multiplication computes all weighted connections together, then a bias shifts each result.

A non-linear activation changes those results before the next layer. Without that bend, many stacked layers would collapse into one linear calculation.
common_mistakes: Every layer stores only words and never numbers.
Training keeps all weights fixed forever.
Adding layers guarantees a correct answer without data.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Pass a Row Through a Layer” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Neural networks are the shared foundation of modern image, language, speech, and recommendation systems.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Pass a Row Through a Layer” situation, explain Neural Networks without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
